chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever clothes one of the poor Muslims with a garment to cover his nakedness, or assists him with something from what sustains his livelihood, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will assign to him seventy thousand angels from among the angels who seek forgiveness for every sin he has committed until the Trumpet is blown.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for clothing the poor in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration linking the physical act of clothing the needy to a massive celestial intercession, where seventy thousand angels seek forgiveness for every sin committed by the donor until the Trumpet is blown. This emphasizes the cumulative and enduring nature of charitable reward in Shia tradition, extending beyond mere material aid to spiritual purification. The magnitude of angelic attendance underscores the high status of sustaining the believer's dignity and livelihood.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Safwan, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who clothes someone from the poor Muslims with a cloth from bareness, or assists him with something from what he lives on from his life, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Allocate with him seven thousand angels from the Angels seeking Forgiveness for every sin he had committed up to the Blowing into the trumpet (Day of Judgement)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Safwan from abu Hamza from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever provides a poor Muslim with clothes for covering and assists him in means of his living, as reward Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, assigns seventy thousand angels to pray and ask forgiveness up to the time of the sounding of the trumpet (Day of Judgment) for every sin that he may have committed.’”
